content.text: Confirmed: "Company" = Clear Capital (our party), "Contractor" = RadialSpark. My investigation found no MFN language anywhere in the agreement.

input.quote: During the term of this Agreement, Company agrees to compensate Contractor as set forth in each Statement of Work. Contractor will be compensated on a time and materials.
input.rationale:
The Agreement contains no most-favoured-nation obligation of any kind, and none burdening us. Pricing is set exclusively per-Statement of Work on a time-and-materials basis (§ 3(a), p0013), with invoicing mechanics in § 3(b) (p0014); neither creates any parity, price-matching, or best-terms commitment. Targeted searches for "no less favorable", "most favored", and regex patterns covering favourable/favorable, most-favoured-nation, best price/pricing, matching third-party offers, other customers, exclusivity, preferred provider and comparable terms returned no MFN language anywhere in the document, and full reads of § 1 (Purpose of Engagement) and § 3 (Contractor's Compensation) — the sections where such a term would sit — confirm its absence. Confirmed from the preamble (p0002) that "Company" is Clear Capital (our party) and "Contractor" is RadialSpark, so there is no risk of a mis-directed reading.

This is the preferred position: no MFN obligation on Customer. Note this is not a "missing" finding — the rule expects the absence of such a clause, so absence is full compliance rather than a gap to fill; we would only flag if we were required to extend RadialSpark our best third-party terms. Separately noted but not flagged here: § 3(b) permits the Contractor to "change rates with 30 days notice to Company" without a cap. That is an uncapped price-uplift concern belonging to the pricing/price-increase rule, not an MFN parity obligation, and flagging it under this rule would double-count the same commercial term. No redline proposed.
